author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

title: Reader can narrow the veterinarian list to one specialty by address
summary: Both veterinarian list surfaces, the HTML directory and the machine-readable list, accept an optional specialty in the address and return only veterinarians holding it. Matching is whole-name and case-insensitive; a blank value means no filter.
acceptance_criteria: Given /vets.html?specialty=<name>, only veterinarians holding that specialty are listed, and pagination applies to the filtered list.
Given /vets?specialty=<name>, the JSON document lists only veterinarians holding that specialty.
On both surfaces, a specialty differing from a held specialty only by letter case matches it.
On both surfaces, only the start of a specialty name (a prefix) matches no veterinarian.
On both surfaces, a specialty no veterinarian holds yields HTTP 200 with the normal page or JSON document and an empty vet list.
On both surfaces, an empty or whitespace-only specialty behaves as if the parameter were absent.
Pagination links on a filtered HTML page carry the specialty, so every page of the filtered directory stays filtered.
Without the parameter, both surfaces behave as today (REQ-VET-001, REQ-VET-004; covered by the existing tests).
Neither surface gains a form, dropdown, or other page control for the filter.
non_goals: Free-text veterinarian search (NG-9, narrowed, still declines it).
Any visible filter control (form, dropdown, link list) on either surface; owner said one may come as a follow-up request.
Filtering by more than one specialty at once, or by any other attribute.

PRD changes: NG-9 narrowed (scope_overrides); fresh REQ-VET-004 reinstates the /vets JSON surface as supported, already satisfied by existing behavior and test showResourcesVetList; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn, its Superseded entry now points to REQ-VET-004; REQ-VET-001 edge case 2 (known defect) marked resolved. author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the vet feature package's controller-to-repository shape (system-design § Overview, ADR 2026-07-31 feature-package organization): one derived query pair on VetRepository plus an optional request parameter on both VetController routes. No new module, type, or pattern. The NG-9 narrowing (non-goal ADR 2026-11-05) admits the slice. Adjustments written this dispatch: VetController/VetRepository/Vet/Specialty/Vets/CacheConfiguration Contracts rows now cite REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004; the 'machine-readable route serves no requirement' Known Defects row is removed (REQ-VET-004 reinstates the surface); a new § Scale and Load section records the vet rows; Security Context names the specialty input; two Threat Model rows added. Normalization: the controller strips the value and treats blank as absent, per architecture-principles § Web controller row (normalization is binding) and the OwnerController last-name precedent — this settles the PRD's open question (1). Basis for the covering code: grep and file reads (IDE oracle not connected — weaker basis).
integration_points: Entry points /vets.html and /vets bind one optional String request parameter 'specialty' (a request-scoped scalar; no persisted type is bound). Absent, empty, or whitespace-only after strip() dispatches to the existing unfiltered, cached methods unchanged.

VetRepository gains a paged and an unpaged derived query matching Specialty name by whole-name, case-insensitive equality (Spring Data 'Distinct ... SpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase' form, or an equivalent parameterized JPQL equality on upper-cased names). Neither carries @Cacheable.

Repository boundary double: the real Spring Data JPA repository on embedded H2 with the seed data, driven through MockMvc (sanctioned transport stand-in). Case-insensitive, whole-name, prefix, and unknown-specialty matching are repository behavior a stub cannot observe, so every new REQ-VET-003 test runs against the real repository. Existing @MockitoBean tests in VetControllerTests stay as they are; no new stub is sanctioned.
vetList.html pagination links render the specialty as a Thymeleaf link-expression parameter, e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, emitted only when a filter is active.

patterns.description: strip() normalization of a search parameter in the controller before querying
paged Spring Data derived query taking a Pageable

risks.risk: Template expression injection: the existing links use '__${...}__' preprocessing; feeding the caller's specialty through preprocessing evaluates attacker text as an expression.
risks.mitigation: Pass the specialty only as an encoded link-expression parameter (system-design § Threat Model, template-expression-injection row; security-principles trust boundary at request input).

risks.risk: Unbounded vet-cache growth if filtered methods are @Cacheable, since the JCache config sets no size limit and keys would be caller-chosen strings.
risks.mitigation: Filtered reads are uncached (system-design § Scale and Load, filtered vet list row; § Threat Model cache-growth row).

risks.risk: Specialty-filtered vet list path scales with data (system-design § Scale and Load, filtered row: bounded).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: one query, distinct veterinarians, paged on HTML, whole list on JSON.

risks.risk: A fetch join on the filter would truncate each veterinarian's specialty set to the matched one; a plain join without DISTINCT can duplicate a veterinarian and skew page counts.
risks.mitigation: Filter through a plain join with DISTINCT; specialties keep loading through the existing eager mapping (system-design § Persistence, open-in-view disabled; VetRepository Contracts row 'return each veterinarian once').

risks.risk: Case-insensitivity must hold on H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL, whose collations differ (system-design § Persistence); the test suite only runs H2.
risks.mitigation: Compare both sides in one letter case in the query (IgnoreCase / upper()), never rely on column collation. Use equality, never LIKE, so '%' and '_' in the value match literally.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; skipped. Owner absent (intake line 1); narrowest readings recorded, not asked: (1) surrounding spaces on a non-blank value are stripped, per the binding normalization rule above; (2) a repeated specialty parameter is out of scope — Spring binds it as the comma-joined value, which matches no specialty and yields an empty 200 list; no special handling; (3) a page number past the end, or below 1, behaves as the unfiltered route does today; (4) filtered page order follows the unfiltered route's repository default. No ADR written: the uncached-filter and case-folding choices are contained in this slice and recorded as one clause on their current-state lines. Relayed product-expert request done: docs/adr/README.md index gains the row for docs/adr/2026-11-05-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md. § Scale and Load did not exist in system-design.md; it was added with the vet rows only, other features' rows stay for the slices that touch them.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the request-supplied specialty reaches the database only through Spring Data derived queries `findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String)` and `(String, Pageable)` (VetRepository.java diff), which bind the value as a parameter; no query text is concatenated. IgnoreCase without Like/Containing derives an equality comparison, so `%` and `_` in the input are literals, not wildcards.

Template injection removed, not added: the five pagination links in src/main/resources/templates/vets/vetList.html lines 30-52 replace `@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}` preprocessing with link-expression parameters `@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}`, so the request-derived specialty is URL-encoded by Thymeleaf and never evaluated as an expression. `grep -F -e '__$' -r src/main/resources/templates` shows no remaining preprocessing in vetList.html; the hits in ownersList.html, ownerDetails.html, layout.html and the field fragments are pre-existing and untouched by this change.

Cross-site scripting: the specialty value is rendered only inside `th:href` link expressions (escaped attribute output); `grep -F -e utext -r src/main/resources/templates` returns no hits, so default escaping stays on everywhere.

Resource exhaustion: both new repository methods are deliberately uncached (VetRepository.java Javadoc: 'Uncached, because the name is caller-chosen and would grow the unbounded vet cache'), so a caller cannot grow the `vets` cache with arbitrary specialty names; the existing cached `findAll` paths are unchanged.

Input validation at the boundary: VetController.requestedSpecialty strips the parameter and treats blank as absent, matching the PRD rule at docs/prd.md:134; an unknown name yields an empty result rather than an error, so no exception message carrying the input reaches the error page.

Surface: no new endpoint and no mass-assignment target; the change adds an optional `@RequestParam String` to the existing GET routes `/vets.html` and `/vets`, both read-only, so the exposed surface stays at the baseline in docs/security-principles.md.
No secrets: the diff adds no token, password, secret, key, or credential-like literal (diff read in full).

Supply chain: build.gradle and gradle/ are unchanged (`git status --short build.gradle gradle` empty). Resolved runtime versions from `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath`: Spring Boot 4.1.2, jackson-databind 3.1.7, thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE. No NVD scan ran, the standing gap listed in docs/security-principles.md § Standing Gaps.
